title: Concrete Pump Motor kW vs Catalogue Output — Same m³/h, Different Drive
seoTitle: Concrete Pump Motor kW vs Output | Pinjin Xingtai
description: Electric 15 is 15 kW and Electric 20 is 22 kW; both list 8–10 m³/h. Motor kW is the drive cell, not a second output table. This page does not repeat the output m³/h buyer guide. Compare printed kW, pressure and distance on the same row, then inquire.
secondaryKeywords: concrete pump motor power vs output

answerBlock.what: Pinjin prints motor (or engine) power and theoretical output on the same product row. They are two cells, not a formula we will invent. Electric 15: 15 kW, 8–10 m³/h. Electric 20: 22 kW, 8–10 m³/h. Same output band, different kW, different mass (450 kg vs 900 kg) and different pipe (100–125 mm vs 80 mm). Electric 40: 45 kW, 21 m³/h. HBT8018: 132 kW, 60 m³/h. The older output-m³/h article already covers how to read the volume cell. This page only stops buyers from treating kW as a second m³/h table or from interpolating an unpublished 18 kW SKU.
answerBlock.who: Buyers comparing two electric trailer rows who saw the same 8–10 m³/h and need the printed kW, mass and pipe cells — not a made-up efficiency ratio.
factors: Read kW and m³/h from the same model row; do not mix columns
Electric 15 and Electric 20 share 8–10 m³/h but not kW, mass or pipe DN
No published kW-to-m³/h conversion formula on Pinjin pages
Grid kVA and diesel kW are site facts — see electric vs diesel

faqs.question: If Electric 20 has more kW, why does it list the same 8–10 m³/h as Electric 15?
faqs.answer: Because output and motor power are separate catalogue cells. Electric 15 is 15 kW, 450 kg, 100–125 mm pipe. Electric 20 is 22 kW, 900 kg, 80 mm pipe. We do not publish an efficiency ratio that turns 22 kW into a higher m³/h than printed. Compare the whole row, then inquire.

faqs.question: Can I order a 18 kW motor on Electric 15 to get more output?
faqs.answer: No 18 kW SKU is listed. Electric 15 is 15 kW. Electric 20 is 22 kW. Electric 40 is 45 kW. Unpublished motor swaps are not factory specs on this site. If you need 21 m³/h, that is the Electric 40 row (45 kW), not a restamped Electric 15.

faqs.question: Does this page replace the output m³/h selection article?
faqs.answer: No. That article already explains how to read the volume cell against pour size. This page is only motor kW versus that cell, using the printed pairs. Do not duplicate the pour-size table here.
